steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What code is needed to find the value of a status bar?


Solution:

.value should be added outside of the parentheses in each getStatusBarAttachedTo function in the onOverlap event.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ What function creates a status bar above a sprite on screen?


Solution:

statusbar.attachToSprite(sprite) should be added inside the createStatusBar function.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which timer function allows a repeated event only once per time interval?


Solution:

The timer.after function should be replaced with the timer.throttle function inside the conditional of the sendFood function.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which timer function runs a chunk of code after a certain amount of time has passed?


Solution:

The destroyAllSpritesOfKind function, printDialog function, and startGame function calls should be placed inside of a timer.after function with 2000 set passed as the time argument.
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code to create a working project!


When the project starts, the titleText image asset should be displayed for 2 seconds before transitioning to the directions.


When the game starts, each Monkey sprite should have a status bar above its head.


When the A button is pressed, the Player sprite should only be able to send a Projectile sprite every 500 milliseconds.


When a Projectile sprite overlaps a Monkey sprite, the Monkey sprite’s status bar should increase by 1. The monkeyFull function should be called when the status bar’s value is equal to 4.


Use the functions in the code menu to create a working version of this project!

subgroups.title: Debugging Timers and Status Bars
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 10 of Brown Belt! Before you create your final Brown Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 10:

badges.title: Extension Explorer
badges.description: Use the minimap, status bar, timer, and raycasting extensions to enhance a project.

badges.title: Bird’s Eye View
badges.description: Create and pin a minimap displaying a smaller representation of sprites and the tilemap in a corner of the screen.

badges.title: Gauging the Action
badges.description: Make something happen based on the value of a status bar.

badges.title: Wait for the Signal
badges.description: Use throttle to delay an action in a game.

badges.title: Right on Cue
badges.description: Run a chunk of code after a certain amount of time has passed.

badges.title: In-Depth Image
badges.description: Create a 3D version of a tilemap from a sprite’s perspective.

badges.title: Points of View
badges.description: Toggle between 3D and top-down views of a tilemap.
